content.title: What is the Fanatics Flag Football Classic? Rosters, how to watch and more
content.text: Who can say no to some football during March Madness? That's right, several NFL stars are about to take the field in March, ranging from Philadelphia Eagles stars Jalen Hurts, DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley to Cincinnati Bengals QB1 Joe Burrow to former standouts Odell Beckham Jr. and Luke Kuechley. Oh, and Tom Brady is back to toss dimes, too. It's all part of a new exhibition called the Fanatics Flag Football Classic. So, what is the event and where will it be available to watch? Here's everything to know: MORE ON FLAG FOOTBALL What is the Fanatics Flag Football Classic? The Fanatics Flag Football Classic is an upcoming event where NFL stars, celebrities and flag football veterans will take the field in a mini round-robin tournament to spotlight the sport in the build up to the 2028 LA Olympics. The action will follow modified Olympic-style flag football rules, featuring two 15-minute halves with a running clock on a 50 x 25-yard field. When and what time is the Fanatics Flag Football Classic? The event is on Saturday, March 21. The action will run from 4 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. ET/1 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. PT. Where is the Fanatics Flag Football Classic? The event will take place at BMO Stadium, home of MLS side LAFC in Los Angeles. It was originally slated for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, but was relocated amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. What are the rosters for the Fanatics Flag Football Classic? Three teams will compete in a four-game round-robin tournament, where the top two will advance to the championship match. Brady and Hurts are captains of Founders FFC, while Burrows and Washington Commanders QB1 Jayden Daniels captain Wildcats FFC. The third team is the U.S. men's national flag football team, anchored by QB Darrell “Housh” Doucette III and DB/WR Aamir Brown. Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos will coach the Founders, while San Francisco 49ers' Kyle Shanahan is the Wildcats' lead coach. New Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh will be a defensive specialist for the two sides. Here's the roster breakdown: Founders FFC Tom Brady, retired QB Jalen Hurts, QB, Philadelphia Eagles DeVonta Smith, WR, Philadelphia Eagles Ashton Jeanty, RB, Las Vegas Raiders Antoine Winfield Jr., S, Tampa Bay Buccaneers Alvin Kamara, RB, New Orleans Saints Rob Gronkowski, retired TE Stefon Diggs, WR, free agent Damar Hamlin, S, free agent Von Miller, DE, free agent Patrick Peterson, retired DB Terence Crawford, retired boxer Wildcats FFC Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Bengals Jayden Daniels, QB, Washington Commanders Davante Adams, WR, Los Angeles Rams Saquon Barkley, RB, Philadelphia Eagles Derwin James Jr., S, Los Angeles Chargers Kyle Juszczyk, FB, San Francisco 49ers Jalen Ramsey, DB, Pittsburgh Steelers Odell Beckham Jr., WR, free agent DeAndre Hopkins, WR, free agent Luke Kuechly, retired LB IShowSpeed, influencer Logan Paul, WWE star and influencer U.S. men's national team Darrell Doucette III, QB Nico Casares, QB Laderrick “Pablo” Smith, WR/QB Aamir Brown, DB/WR Tyler Davis, WR/DB Velton Brown Jr., WR/DB Ja'Deion High, WR/DB Isaiah Calhoun, DB/WR Jamie Kennedy, DB/WR Mike Daniels, DB/WR Laval Davis, DE/WR Shawn Theard Jr., DE/WR Jorge Cascudo (head coach) How to watch the Fanatics Flag Football Classic on TV, online The action will be broadcast on Fox Sports. Fox One and Tubi will stream the games. Actor and comedian Kevin Hart and internet personality Druski will host the event, with Travis Scott expected to perform. 0:59Snoop Dogg's 2028 Olympics dream team for flag football We had the exclusive opportunity to sit down with Mr. Olympics himself, Snoop Dogg, to share his ultimate dream team in flag football for the 2028 Olympics.
